title: Repurposing Dna-Binding Proteins as Molecular Actuators in Synthetic Systems Through Proximity-Driven DNA Reactions
authors: Elena Spezzani; Luca Capelli; Sofia Marzari; Alessandro Bertucci
one_liner_zh: 该文利用邻近驱动的DNA链置换反应将DBP（含TF如EGR1、YY1、p53）的DNA识别转化为合成分子系统的功能输出，虽非直接建模TF-DNA互作机制，但展示了蛋白-DNA识别与核酸反应网络的耦合，对TF-DNA结合的功能化应用和分子设计有借鉴价值。
abstract: DNA-binding proteins (DBPs) play central roles in gene regulation by recognizing specific DNA sequences, yet their function in synthetic molecular systems is typically limited to transcriptional control or sequence-specific binding. Here we describe a proximity-driven molecular framework that couples DBP–DNA recognition to DNA strand displacement reactions, enabling DNA-binding proteins to act as sequence-selective inputs for synthetic nucleic acid reaction pathways without modification of the protein scaffold. In our design, protein binding induces spatial colocalization of DNA components, triggering conditional generation of functional nucleic acid outputs through proximity-mediated strand displacement. Using representative DBPs, including EGR1, YY1, and p53, we connect protein recognition to DNA strand displacement, activation of a fluorogenic RNA aptamer, regulation of CRISPR–Cas12a and Cas13 activity, and coordination of multistep CRISPR cascades. A defining feature of this strategy is the decoupling of molecular recognition from downstream function, which avoids structural and thermodynamic constraints associated with switch-based designs. These results demonstrate a general proximity-based approach for integrating DNA-binding proteins into programmable molecular architectures.
abstract_zh: DNA结合蛋白（DNA-binding proteins, DBPs）通过识别特定DNA序列在基因调控中发挥核心作用，然而它们在合成分子系统中的功能通常仅限于转录控制或序列特异性结合。在此，我们描述了一种邻近驱动的分子框架，将DBP–DNA识别与DNA链置换反应耦合，使DNA结合蛋白能够作为合成核酸反应途径的序列选择性输入，而无需修饰蛋白质支架。在我们的设计中，蛋白质结合诱导DNA组分的空间共定位，通过邻近介导的链置换触发功能性核酸输出的条件性生成。利用代表性DBPs，包括EGR1、YY1和p53，我们将蛋白质识别连接到DNA链置换、荧光RNA适配体的激活、CRISPR–Cas12a和Cas13活性的调控，以及多步CRISPR级联的协调。该策略的一个显著特征是将分子识别与下游功能解耦，从而避免了基于开关设计相关的结构和热力学约束。这些结果展示了一种基于邻近效应的通用方法，用于将DNA结合蛋白整合到可编程分子架构中。
